subject.title: fix(gateway): reject invalid session history limit with 400 instead of coercing to 1

question: Should the shipped session-history HTTP endpoint change malformed explicit `limit` values from a successful one-message response to HTTP 400?
rationale: The patch is technically narrow, but it deliberately removes a released fallback behavior on a public HTTP surface, so maintainers must accept the compatibility impact.

options.title: Adopt strict validation
options.body: Accept HTTP 400 for malformed explicit limits after live proof confirms invalid, normal, and oversized request behavior.

options.title: Preserve released coercion
options.body: Keep the existing one-message fallback and close or redesign this PR if malformed-client compatibility is more important than strict validation.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict validation
recommendation.body: Accept HTTP 400 for malformed explicit limits after live proof confirms invalid, normal, and oversized request behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the endpoint and its limit-handling contract, providing the strongest available feature-history signal.
